license.name: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International
facts: The repository LICENSE is the only stated term found; the model weights are bundled in the same repository and no separate weights-licence or weights-terms file exists.
Creative Commons advises against using CC licences for software, but that advice is not by itself a determination that CC-BY-4.0 is incompatible with AGPLv3.
license.concern: Whether the repository LICENSE covers the bundled weights, and how redistribution would be treated, is UNRESOLVED and must be reviewed under SPEC.md 25.5 before any release use. The absence of a patent grant is a fact, not proof of any AGPLv3 conflict. No blanket compatibility determination is made here; benchmark-only non-runtime study is all this evidence supports.

models.loader: src/BeatNet/BeatNet.py loads models/model_{1,2,3}_weights.pt via torch.load(..., map_location default) into BDA(272,150,2)
models.sha256_provenance: sha256 computed locally on 2026-10-07 from the PINNED upstream commit, not from the mutable branch
models.note: The three 1.54 MiB CRNN state dicts are loaded by BeatNet.py; the repo also ships duplicate model-{1,2,3}.pt variants. All were trained on mastered commercial datasets; the README states the streaming recipe assumes mastered songs.
models.scratch_only: the weight files were downloaded to scratch only to compute sha256; they are not committed and are not part of any release artifact

stream.execution: microphone, one 20 ms hop at a time, PF causal
stream.lookahead_note: source comment: centred training window causes 0.084 s delay that 'needs to be fixed'; plus 5-hop warmup (100 ms) before first non-zero activation

realtime.execution: file read one 20 ms hop at a time, PF causal
realtime.lookahead_note: the feature window for hop N spans [hop*(N-2), hop*N + win_length], i.e. the 64 ms window extends ~64 ms beyond the current hop; an observation is therefore causal only once that window has completed — this is not zero-lookahead, and per_chunk availability must be the window end

online.execution: whole file in one batch for activations, then PF over the whole sequence; README claims identical outcomes to realtime
online.lookahead_note: causal algorithm, but the whole file must be read first, so per-event causal availability cannot be measured; suitable for corpus accuracy, not for the availability half of a SPEC 12.3 claim

offline.execution: whole file in one batch, then madmom DBNDownBeatTrackingProcessor (non-causal)
offline.lookahead_note: not causal; PF is the causal path

hard_imports_even_for_causal_path: src/BeatNet/BeatNet.py: from madmom.features import DBNDownBeatTrackingProcessor (top-level, so madmom is required even for PF)

dependency_blockers.summary: madmom 0.16.1 (2018, unmaintained) is a hard dependency of the causal path and cannot be installed/imported unmodified on Python 3.13
measured: pip install madmom==0.16.1 (isolated build): 'ModuleNotFoundError: No module named Cython' while getting requirements (madmom sdist has no pyproject build-system requires for Cython)
pip install 'numpy<1.24' (era-appropriate for madmom): build fails with "AttributeError: module 'pkgutil' has no attribute 'ImpImporter'" (removed in Python 3.12)
with modern Cython 3.3.0 + numpy 2.5.3 + scipy 1.18.1 and --no-build-isolation, madmom 0.16.1 DOES build (wheel 21806757 bytes)

even then, importing any required madmom module fails: first 'ModuleNotFoundError: No module named pkg_resources' (fixed by setuptools<81), then 'ImportError: cannot import name MutableSequence from collections' (removed in Python 3.10), then, after a scratch-only collections shim, 'AttributeError: module numpy has no attribute float' (removed in numpy 1.24)
dependency_blockers.conclusion: madmom 0.16.1 simultaneously requires the numpy<1.24 API and a Python that can build numpy<1.24; Python 3.13 satisfies neither. Running BeatNet here would require either patching unmaintained madmom source or provisioning an older interpreter.

dependency_blockers.summary: PyPI BeatNet 1.1.3 hard-pins numba==0.54.1, which predates Python 3.13
measured: numba 0.54.1 (2021) supports Python <= 3.9; no cp313 wheel exists and the source needs llvmlite 0.37 which does not build on 3.13
dependency_blockers.note: The git tree (setup.py version 1.2.0) drops the numba pin, but the last published PyPI release (1.1.3) carries it.

dependency_blockers.summary: Default PyPI torch wheel exceeds the 500 MB download budget on its own
measured: torch 2.14.1 cp313 manylinux_2_28_x86_64.whl = 554.6 MB (PyPI default Linux wheel, CUDA-enabled runtime payload)
dependency_blockers.note: The CPU-only wheel from download.pytorch.org is much smaller (see budget) but requires the extra index and torch==2.6.0+cpu rather than what BeatNet's unconstrained 'torch' resolves to.

dependency_blockers.summary: No compatible Python interpreter is present and no GPU is available
measured: only /usr/bin/python3 -> Python 3.13.5; python3.9/3.10/3.11/3.12 absent; no pyenv/conda
dependency_blockers.conclusion: A CPU-only causal benchmark would require provisioning a separate supported interpreter first; that is outside this bounded feasibility review and carries its own download/disk budget.

selected_cp313_wheels_bytes.note: plus librosa/matplotlib/tensorboard/mido/pyyaml/pytest and their transitive wheels; a full closure is well over 300 MB of downloads and, once installed, torch alone unpacks to roughly 1 GB

measured_venv_after_numpy_scipy_cython_m.note: the review venv contained Cython, numpy, scipy, madmom (built), setuptools<81, mido, packaging, wheel, pip; torch was deliberately not installed

verdict: INFEASIBLE now within the stated environment/budget without either provisioning an additional supported Python interpreter or patching unmaintained third-party source. No BeatNet accuracy, latency, CPU or startup number is produced by this review.
